title: TriSpec: Ternary Speculative Decoding via Lightweight Proxy Verification
claim: Standard verification always invokes the expensive model; adding a cheap trusted proxy lets it handle easy cases and escalate only when uncertain.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, token rows stacked top-down with check/cross marks
description: Three side-by-side panels show token-level verification in speculative decoding. Panel (a) 'Standard SD' stacks a blue Draft box, a green Target box, and token rows x1–x6 and x2–x7, with green dotted links, green check marks for accepted tokens, and a red cross at the first rejection. Output 'New Tokens' x2–x5 appears at the bottom. Panel (b) 'TriSpec Case I' adds a yellow Proxy row between Draft and Target. Gold stars mark trusted proxy verdicts, and the Target box is greyed out and dashed because it is skipped. Panel (c) 'TriSpec Case II' shows a red question mark for an untrusted proxy verdict, which activates the Target row to verify the remaining tokens. A legend explains Passed, Failed, Trusted and Untrusted. A downward arrow at the left of each panel marks the flow, and the colors blue, yellow and green identify the models.
caption: Comparison of (a) standard SD and (b-c) TriSpec. In (b), the proxy remains trusted at the first rejection, enabling local correction without invoking the target. In (c), the proxy becomes untrusted before the first rejection, so the remaining draft tokens are escalated to the target for authoritative verification. A margin-based criterion determines whether proxy verification is trusted.
abstract: Inference efficiency in Large Language Models (LLMs) is fundamentally limited by their serial, autoregressive generation, especially as reasoning becomes a key capability and response sequences grow longer. Speculative decoding (SD) offers a powerful solution, providing significant speed-ups through its lightweight drafting and parallel verification mechanism. While existing work has nearly saturated improvements in draft effectiveness and efficiency, this paper advances SD from a new yet critical perspective: the verification cost. We propose TriSpec, a novel ternary SD framework that, at its core, introduces a lightweight proxy to significantly reduce computational cost by approving easily verifiable draft sequences and engaging the full target model only when encountering uncertain tokens. TriSpec can be integrated with state-of-the-art SD methods like EAGLE-3 to further reduce verification costs, achieving greater acceleration. Extensive experiments on the Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen/LLaMA families show that TriSpec achieves up to 35% speedup over standard SD, with up to 50% fewer target model invocations while maintaining comparable accuracy.
